title: Unblock tenant fairness with adaptive time-slicing to prevent queue starvation under mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Customer escalations from three accounts (one Hosted, one Dedicated, one Private) reported recurring service slowness where short requests experienced severe latency spikes and timeouts during mixed-length traffic waves. Root cause is an admission scheduling pathology: admission leases and prefetching combine to create persistent token slabs held by long-context flows, leading to queue starvation for latency-sensitive short requests. The problem is amplified on Private during rolling upgrades because an admission-lease renewal race sometimes left stale slots in the admission reservoir.

Scope:
- Affects continuous batching runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Observed as short-request tail latency > 5x baseline and customer requests dropping due to client-side timeouts.
- Reproducible with a mixed workload PR (short chat completions + long document summarizations) hitting the prefetch threshold.

Goal:
Design and ship a fix that restores tenant-level fairness and eliminates starvation without regressing throughput for long-context workloads. Provide monitoring/guardrails to detect recurrence and safe rollback paths for Dedicated/Private customers.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Adaptive time-slicing: allocate per-tenant time-slices within the admission window (token-slabs) that cap continuous token acquisition per-tenant in a sliding time horizon. Short requests can preempt after their slice and be scheduled promptly.
2) Prefetch quarantine: introduce a grace window where prefetch requests are not allowed to consume admission tokens immediately; instead they are enqueued with lower admission priority and promoted after a short delay if capacity remains.
3) Admission-lease harden: fix lease renewal race in Private upgrade path by making lease state durable across coordinator restarts (idempotent lease reclaims + metadata tombstones).
4) Metrics and alerts: add tenant-level fairness score, admitted-token-age histogram, and prefetch-promotion rate to Grafana dashboards; create alert when short-request tail ratio exceeds threshold.

Trade-offs considered:
- Stronger limits (hard caps) would immediately restore latency but hurt throughput and model utilization for long jobs; adaptive slices balance both but are more complex to reason about.
- Prefetch quarantine adds a small extra latency for beneficial prefetches; chosen window is conservative (50-150ms) to avoid harming user experience.
- Durable lease fixes for Private require a migration path for older control-plane versions; will be gated behind runtime-1.22 and an opt-in upgrade for on-prem customers.

Rollout plan:
- Canary in Hosted (us-west1) with 5% of traffic for 48 hours.
- Dedicated beta with a single reserved pool in staging, then two customer pools in prod behind feature flag.
- Private: provide patch bundle + upgrade instructions; offer to perform automated migration for enterprise customers.

Backout plan:
- Feature flag to disable adaptive time-slicing and quarantine quickly across all environments.
- Immediate rollback to previous admission algorithm if imbalance worsens.

Acceptance criteria:
- Short-request p50/p95 latency restored to within 1.2x of baseline under mixed workload test harness.
- No more than 2% loss in tokens/sec throughput for long-context workloads at baseline load.
- Dashboards reporting fairness score >= 0.85 for test tenants during canary.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial customer report triaged. Collected Grafana traces and flamegraphs from hosted region; short-request tail shows repeated admission wait cycles. Opened reproducer and started triage.

2026-03-11 - Diego Alvarez: Reproducer validated locally. Confirmed prefetch requests are visible in admission logs as immediate token consumers. Observed admission lease timestamp anomalies during simulated control-plane restart in Private.

2026-03-12 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype adaptive time-slicing added to local continuous-batcher. Short-request p95 dropped from 420ms -> 78ms in harness. Created PR #10542 for review with unit/integration tests.

2026-03-12 - Priya Singh (SRE): Added temporary Grafana panels for admitted-token-age and per-tenant admitted-rate. Verified canary trend looks promising; no apparent throughput regression at 60% load.

2026-03-13 - Code review: Platform runtime team requested stronger invariants around token accounting and explicit instrumentation for lease handoffs. Diego updated PR with a reconciliation pass that runs every 5s to detect leaks.

2026-03-13 - Legal/Privacy review: Verified no customer data touches the new control-plane metrics; marked security_review_required=false. Noted we must still update Private upgrade notes for enterprise customers.

2026-03-14 - QA: End-to-end tests on Dedicated staging passed. Observed one flaky test in prefetch promotion logic; added deterministic delay and retry which stabilized it. Preparing canary config for Hosted.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez: Pushed feature-flag gate and rollback endpoints. Canary scheduled to start 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC and run for 48 hours. Notified support and account teams for the three impacted customers.
